title: FAA UAP record 237UAP00215
what_is_it: FAA SKYWATCH incident report documenting a pilot observation of an unidentified aerial phenomenon.
core_summary: On 12 February 2023, a commercial Boeing 747-8 (callsign ICV93PK) flying eastbound at 35,000 feet reported an unidentified aerial phenomenon 43 nautical miles northwest of Burlington, Vermont. The crew observed a light estimated above 60,000 feet moving erratically, with three lights forming a triangle pattern that merged into one light repeatedly. A second aircraft heading north to Montreal reported the same observation.

public_headline: Boeing 747 crew and second aircraft report triangular lights over Vermont
public_tldr: An FAA incident report records that on 12 February 2023, a commercial Boeing 747-8 crew flying at 35,000 feet observed an erratically moving light estimated above 60,000 feet near Burlington, Vermont. Three lights repeatedly formed a triangle and merged into one; a second aircraft independently reported the same observation. The case was closed with no explanation provided.
public_narrative:
This is a single-page FAA SKYWATCH incident report filed on 12 February 2023 at 08:25 UTC. It documents what the crew of a commercial Boeing 747-8, operating under callsign ICV93PK on a cargo route from Chicago O'Hare to Luxembourg, observed while flying eastbound at 35,000 feet.

Approximately 43 nautical miles northwest of Burlington, Vermont, the crew reported a light estimated to be above 60,000 feet moving in an erratic pattern. They described three lights that appeared to form a triangle shape, then merged into a single light — a process that repeated several times.

A second aircraft, flying northbound toward Montreal, independently reported seeing the same phenomenon. This multi-witness aspect is notable: two separate crews in different locations observed the same thing.

The FAA's Aviation Weather Office (AWO) was notified. The case status is listed as "Closed" — but the report contains no resolution, no follow-up investigation details, and no explanation for what the crews observed. No radar data or instrument readings are referenced; all observations are visual only.

The document is brief and administrative in nature. It records the event but does not analyse or explain it.
public_caveats: This is a single-page report with no follow-up investigation or resolution — 'Closed' does not mean 'explained'.
All observations are visual only; no radar data, photographs, or instrument readings are referenced in the document.
The altitude estimate of the phenomenon (above 60,000 feet) is the crew's visual estimate, not a measured value.
The tail number field is blank, which limits independent verification of the reporting aircraft.
Two crews reported the same observation, but no additional corroboration (ground radar, satellite, etc.) is documented.
